nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the b123d helper module, re-exporting the deterministic build123d domain helpers and shared conventions so the CAD agent loop can import them from a single namespace.
nodes.languageNotes: Python package __init__ acting as a re-export barrel.

nodes.name: conventions.py
nodes.summary: Holds shared build123d conventions, notably a metric coarse-thread pitch table and a coarse_pitch() lookup used by the bolt helper.

nodes.name: domain.py
nodes.summary: Provides deterministic build123d geometry helpers (structural_section for I/H/C beams, spur_gear with true involute teeth, hex_bolt) that the CAD agent loop calls directly and trusts without visual critique.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses build123d BuildPart/BuildSketch context managers plus manual involute-curve math (math.cos/sin/atan2) to generate gear tooth profiles deterministically.

nodes.name: coarse_pitch
nodes.summary: Returns the ISO metric coarse-thread pitch in mm for a given nominal bolt size, falling back to an approximation when the size is not in the lookup table.

nodes.name: structural_section
nodes.summary: Builds an extruded structural steel section (I/H/C beam) from web/flange dimensions using a build123d polyline cross-section, with optional mitre end cuts.

nodes.name: _apply_mitre_b123d
nodes.summary: Applies angled mitre cuts to the ends of a structural section by extruding and subtracting wedge solids at the part extremities.

nodes.name: spur_gear
nodes.summary: Generates a parametric involute spur gear from teeth count, module, width and bore, computing the true involute tooth profile via trigonometric strips before extruding the swept polyline.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines nested helpers (inv, t_at, rot2d, involute_strip, arc_strip) to assemble the involute tooth polygon point-by-point.

nodes.name: hex_bolt
nodes.summary: Builds a hex-head bolt solid from nominal size and length, deriving thread pitch via coarse_pitch and extruding a regular-hexagon head atop a cylindrical shank.

nodes.name: BUILDS.md
nodes.summary: Build-verification checklist for CAD Agent v4.2, listing Tier 0 smoke tests expected to converge on the 7B coder, the text-to-cad benchmark suite invocation, and the workflow for rating good builds into the few-shot store.

nodes.name: PROJECT.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative design document for CAD Agent v4.2 covering architecture, the build123d agentic observe-edit loop, coder routing, learning loop, hardware/model routing, and the tuning surface for changing behavior.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Operator-facing skill guide for CAD Agent v4.2 documenting when to use it, available scripts and commands, the per-build loop, coder routing, the Telegram (Satine) frontend, and verification/learning-loop behavior.

nodes.name: extrude_cut.md
nodes.summary: Capability reference describing how to subtract material via extrude-cut operations (pockets, through-holes, slots, hollow shells), including the BTM JSON pattern and common cut patterns the CAD agent can apply.
nodes.languageNotes: Reference note structured around a single CAD operation with BTM JSON snippets and gotchas; consumed as context by the codegen model rather than rendered for humans.

nodes.name: fillet_chamfer.md
nodes.summary: Capability reference for edge-break operations (fillet and chamfer), covering BTM JSON patterns, edge-selection strategies, and common rounding/beveling patterns used when finishing CAD parts.

nodes.name: mirror.md
nodes.summary: Capability reference for the Mirror feature, explaining its two modes (mirror feature vs mirror part), standard mirror planes, and BTM JSON patterns for building symmetric brackets, gear pairs, and mirrored cuts.

nodes.name: thread_creation.md
nodes.summary: Capability reference for adding threads to a cylindrical face, covering prerequisites, the Onshape built-in Thread feature BTM JSON pattern, a ThreadCreator FeatureScript alternative, and the threaded-lid container pattern.

nodes.name: specs.json
nodes.summary: Text-to-CAD benchmark suite: 10 natural-language part specs with expected geometry hints, used by run_benchmarks.py to score the agent end-to-end.

nodes.name: cad_agent_v4.py
nodes.summary: The central CAD agent: drives the full build123d observe-edit loop (brief -> coder-triage -> codegen -> run/inspect/render -> gemma visual critic -> edit), handles coder model routing (7B<->30B), Onshape STEP upload, and the CLI/Telegram command surface.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-module agent (~1000 LOC) using only the stdlib (urllib, subprocess, ast, tempfile) to talk to Ollama and Onshape; coder model is auto-routed and escalated 7B->30B after repeated failures.

nodes.name: cad_retrieval.py
nodes.summary: The learning-loop retrieval layer: nomic-embed semantic few-shot retrieval over the rated build123d corpus plus fail->fix lesson storage/retrieval, with a cached embedding store and word-overlap fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: Cosine similarity and embeddings computed by hand against a JSONL corpus with a SHA-keyed embedding cache; degrades to lexical word-overlap when the embed model is unavailable.

nodes.name: run_benchmarks.py
nodes.summary: Benchmark harness that runs each text-to-cad spec through cad_agent_v4 as a subprocess, derives geometry from the produced STEP, and writes timestamped pass/fail results.

nodes.name: step
nodes.summary: Runner script that executes generated build123d source in an isolated namespace and exports the resulting solid to a STEP file; invoked as a subprocess by the agent's run_step.
nodes.languageNotes: Extension-less executable Python script; auto-detects the result object by probing common variable names (result/part/shape/body/output).

nodes.name: inspect
nodes.summary: Geometry validation runner that loads a STEP file and reports bounding box, face/solid counts and validity, feeding the agent's inspect-and-revise step.
nodes.languageNotes: Extension-less executable Python CLI; output is line-prefixed (WARN/ERROR) for the agent to parse.

nodes.name: render
nodes.summary: Headless STEP-to-PNG renderer producing a two-panel (isometric + top-down) shaded image for the multimodal critic, drawn with matplotlib Agg and edge-less flat-shaded faces.
nodes.languageNotes: Extension-less Python script using matplotlib Agg + Poly3DCollection; deliberately suppresses triangulation edges so the critic doesn't mistake the tessellation fan for real facets.

nodes.name: bolt.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy Onshape FeatureScript reference snippet demonstrating a bolt; standalone read-only example data, not part of the v4 build123d pipeline.

nodes.name: helix-thread.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy Onshape FeatureScript reference snippet demonstrating a helical thread; standalone read-only example data.

nodes.name: loft.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy Onshape FeatureScript reference snippet demonstrating a loft operation; standalone read-only example data.

nodes.name: revolve.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy Onshape FeatureScript reference snippet demonstrating a revolve operation; standalone read-only example data.

nodes.name: sweep.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy Onshape FeatureScript reference snippet demonstrating a sweep operation; standalone read-only example data.

nodes.name: learned_chair.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy learned FeatureScript artifact for a chair build, captured from an earlier v1 FeatureScript run; standalone read-only reference.

nodes.name: learned_spur_gear_20_teeth__module_2__3_1_meshin.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy learned FeatureScript artifact for a 20-tooth module-2 meshing spur gear pair; standalone read-only reference.

nodes.name: learned_spur_gear.fs
nodes.summary: Legacy learned FeatureScript artifact for a single spur gear; standalone read-only reference.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: The core orchestrator: builds the brief, loads few-shots and lessons, routes the coder, then runs the generate -> step -> inspect -> render -> critique -> edit loop until DONE, finally uploading the STEP to Onshape and persisting session state.

nodes.name: build_brief
nodes.summary: Calls the brief model (qwen3:8b) to turn a free-text spec into a structured JSON build brief (dimensions, operations, optional helper hint).

nodes.name: spec_needs_strong_coder
nodes.summary: LLM triage that decides whether a spec is hard enough to start on the strong 30B coder instead of the fast 7B, parsing a JSON verdict from the brief model.

nodes.name: generate_code
nodes.summary: Generates build123d Python from the brief: either emits a deterministic domain-helper call (bolt/gear/section) or prompts the routed coder model, then strips fences and patches the code.

nodes.name: revise_script
nodes.summary: Asks the coder model to repair failing build123d code given the error/problem and current state, returning patched and fence-stripped source.

nodes.name: decide_or_edit
nodes.summary: Given warnings and the visual critique, asks the coder model to either reply DONE or return an edited script, driving loop termination.

nodes.name: visual_critique
nodes.summary: Renders the STEP to a PNG and sends it with the spec to the multimodal critic model (gemma4:e4b) to judge whether the geometry matches intent.

nodes.name: run_step
nodes.summary: Writes the generated source to disk and invokes the scripts/step runner as a subprocess to produce a STEP file, raising on failure.

nodes.name: run_inspect
nodes.summary: Invokes the scripts/inspect runner as a subprocess and parses its WARN/ERROR lines into geometry warnings.

nodes.name: run_render
nodes.summary: Invokes the scripts/render runner as a subprocess to turn a STEP file into the two-panel critic PNG.

nodes.name: import_step_to_onshape
nodes.summary: Uploads a STEP file to Onshape via multipart, translating it into a real editable Part Studio and polling the translation job, with private-default and auto-public fallback.

nodes.name: _describe_document
nodes.summary: Fetches Onshape document metadata, features and mass properties, then summarizes them via the brief model for the inspect command.

nodes.name: _load_fewshots
nodes.summary: Pulls semantically-similar few-shot examples via cad_retrieval, falling back to keyword-matched rated feedback rows from the feedback JSONL.

nodes.name: store_feedback
nodes.summary: Persists a user rating and the build result into the feedback JSONL, separating gold from rated rows for later few-shot retrieval.

nodes.name: _ollama
nodes.summary: Low-level Ollama generate client with retry, optional images (multimodal) and temperature; the single chokepoint all model calls go through.

nodes.name: preflight
nodes.summary: Pre-run check that Ollama is reachable and the configured brief/coder/critic models are pulled, raising a helpful error otherwise.

nodes.name: _onshape
nodes.summary: Authenticated JSON request helper against the Onshape REST API using basic-auth from configured credentials.

nodes.name: distill_lesson
nodes.summary: Uses the brief model to distill a one-line fail->fix lesson from a build problem and its final code, feeding the lesson store.

nodes.name: _cmd_build
nodes.summary: CLI entry for the build subcommand: parses args (coder mode, fewshots, chat id), runs build, and reports success/failure to stdout and Telegram.

nodes.name: _cmd_inspect
nodes.summary: CLI entry for the inspect subcommand: parses an Onshape URL and prints an LLM summary of the document's geometry.

nodes.name: _cmd_refine
nodes.summary: CLI entry for the refine subcommand (Satine convention): merges an original spec with feedback/history into a refined spec via the brief model.

nodes.name: retrieve
nodes.summary: Semantic few-shot retrieval: embeds the spec, scores corpus rows by cosine similarity (word-overlap prefilter), caches embeddings, and returns the top-n above a score threshold.

nodes.name: retrieve_lessons
nodes.summary: Retrieves the most relevant fail->fix lessons for a spec by cosine similarity over the lessons store, to inject as pitfalls-to-avoid into the prompt.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: Returns the nomic-embed embedding for a text, served from a SHA-keyed cache and falling back gracefully when the embed model is unavailable.

nodes.name: load_corpus
nodes.summary: Loads the rated/gold build123d few-shot corpus from JSONL, skipping malformed rows.

nodes.name: store_lesson
nodes.summary: Appends a distilled fail->fix lesson to the lessons JSONL, deduping against existing lessons and capping the store size.

nodes.name: _word_overlap
nodes.summary: Lexical prefilter/fallback that scores corpus rows by token-set overlap with the spec when embeddings are unavailable or to narrow candidates.

nodes.name: run_one
nodes.summary: Runs a single benchmark spec through cad_agent_v4 as a subprocess, parses the JSON result, derives geometry from any produced STEP, and records pass/fail with timing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Benchmark CLI entry: parses tiers/filters, loads specs.json, runs each spec, aggregates pass counts, and writes timestamped plus latest result files.

nodes.name: derive_geometry
nodes.summary: Loads a produced STEP file with build123d and extracts bounding-box, face count and volume for benchmark scoring.

nodes.name: parse_result
nodes.summary: Extracts the agent's JSON result object from its subprocess stdout, tolerating surrounding log noise.

tour.title: What This System Is
tour.description: Start with PROJECT.md, the authoritative design document for CAD Agent v4.2. It explains the core idea: a local-first agent that turns a natural-language part spec into a real Onshape 3D model, with every inference call served by Ollama and no cloud dependency. Read this first to get the architecture, the build123d observe-edit loop, coder routing, and the learning loop as a mental map before touching any code.

tour.title: How Operators Use It
tour.description: SKILL.md is the operator-facing companion to the design doc: when to reach for the agent, which CLI subcommands exist (build, inspect, refine, rate), how the Telegram frontend Satine drives it, and what the per-build loop does at a high level. BUILDS.md adds the verification angle, listing the Tier 0 smoke tests expected to converge on the fast 7B coder and the benchmark suite used to check the whole pipeline. Together these frame the user-visible contract before we open the engine.

tour.title: The Heart: The Agent Loop
tour.description: cad_agent_v4.py is the center of gravity for the entire project, depended on by the runners, the benchmark harness, and every document. This single ~1000-LOC stdlib-only module orchestrates the whole pipeline and is auto-routed between a fast 7B coder and a strong 30B coder. The build() function inside it is the master control flow: assemble the brief, load few-shots and lessons, route the coder, then iterate generate to step to inspect to render to critique to edit until the model signals DONE, and finally upload to Onshape.
tour.languageLesson: This module talks to Ollama and Onshape using only the Python standard library (urllib, subprocess, ast, tempfile). _ollama() is a single chokepoint helper that every model call funnels through, which makes retries, multimodal images, and temperature uniform across the agent.

tour.title: Brief and Coder Triage
tour.description: Before any geometry exists, the spec becomes a structured plan. build_brief calls the brief model (qwen3:8b) to turn free text into a JSON build brief with dimensions, operations, and an optional helper hint. spec_needs_strong_coder is the routing decision: an LLM triage that judges whether a spec is hard enough to start directly on the 30B coder instead of the fast 7B. This is how the system spends GPU budget wisely, staying fast on easy parts and escalating only when needed.

tour.title: Codegen and the Edit Loop
tour.description: These functions are the inner loop the build() orchestrator drives each turn. generate_code either emits a deterministic domain-helper call (bolt/gear/section) or prompts the routed coder for build123d Python, then strips fences. revise_script repairs code that failed to run, while decide_or_edit takes the geometry warnings plus the visual critique and either returns an edited script or replies DONE to terminate the loop. This is the observe-edit cycle PROJECT.md describes, expressed as code.

tour.title: The Geometry Runners
tour.description: Each loop turn shells out to three standalone subprocess runners that do the actual CAD work in isolation. scripts/step executes the generated build123d source and exports a STEP file; scripts/inspect loads that STEP and reports bounding box, face/solid counts, and validity as WARN/ERROR lines; scripts/render produces a two-panel isometric-plus-top-down PNG for the visual critic. Keeping them as separate executables means a crash in generated code never takes down the agent itself.
tour.languageLesson: These are extension-less executable Python scripts run via subprocess, an isolation boundary. scripts/step auto-detects the result object by probing common variable names (result/part/shape/body/output); scripts/render deliberately suppresses matplotlib triangulation edges so the critic does not mistake the tessellation fan for real facets.

tour.title: Driving the Runners and the Visual Critic
tour.description: Building on the runners from Step 6, these agent methods are the bridge into them. run_step writes the source and invokes scripts/step; run_inspect parses the validation warnings; run_render produces the critic image. visual_critique then sends that PNG plus the original spec to the multimodal critic (gemma4:e4b) to judge whether the geometry actually matches intent. This closed perception loop is what lets a small local model self-correct without a human in the seat.

tour.title: Trusted Deterministic Geometry
tour.description: Some shapes are too precise to leave to an LLM and a vision critic. b123d/domain.py provides deterministic build123d factories the agent calls directly and trusts without visual critique: structural_section for I/H/C beams, spur_gear with true involute teeth, and hex_bolt. When generate_code from Step 5 detects a bolt, gear, or beam, it emits one of these calls instead of prompting the coder, which is why those builds stay fast and correct every time.
tour.languageLesson: domain.py uses build123d BuildPart/BuildSketch context managers plus hand-written involute-curve math (math.cos/sin/atan2). spur_gear defines nested helpers (inv, t_at, rot2d, involute_strip, arc_strip) to assemble the true involute tooth polygon point by point before extruding, geometry an LLM would struggle to get right.

tour.title: Domain Conventions and the Barrel
tour.description: The helpers from Step 8 lean on shared conventions and a clean import surface. b123d/conventions.py holds the metric coarse-thread pitch table exposed via coarse_pitch(), which hex_bolt calls to derive thread pitch from a nominal size. b123d/__init__.py is the package barrel that re-exports the domain helpers and conventions so the agent can import the whole trusted toolkit from one namespace.

tour.title: The Learning Loop
tour.description: cad_retrieval.py is how a small local model punches above its weight. It performs nomic-embed semantic few-shot retrieval over the corpus of rated build123d examples, and stores and retrieves fail-to-fix lessons that get injected into prompts as pitfalls to avoid. retrieve() embeds the spec and ranks the corpus by cosine similarity; retrieve_lessons() surfaces relevant past mistakes. Inside the agent, _load_fewshots and distill_lesson are the hooks that feed this loop on every build.
tour.languageLesson: Embeddings and cosine similarity are computed by hand against a JSONL corpus with a SHA-keyed embedding cache, and the layer degrades to lexical word-overlap when the embed model is unavailable, a graceful-fallback pattern that keeps the agent working offline even if nomic-embed is not loaded.

tour.title: Closing the Loop: Onshape Upload and Feedback
tour.description: Once the loop converges on a good STEP, import_step_to_onshape uploads it via multipart and translates it into a real editable Part Studio, polling the translation job with a private-default and auto-public fallback for free accounts. store_feedback then persists the user's rating into the feedback JSONL, separating gold from rated rows so the retrieval layer from Step 10 gets richer over time. This is where a build becomes a viewable model and also a future few-shot example.

tour.title: Capability Reference Context
tour.description: The codegen model does not work from memory alone. These capability notes are read-only context injected to guide generation: extrude_cut covers pockets, through-holes and shells; fillet_chamfer covers edge breaks; mirror covers symmetry for brackets and gear pairs; thread_creation covers adding threads to cylindrical faces. They teach the model the operation patterns it needs without baking them into the agent code.

tour.title: How It Gets Evaluated
tour.description: Finally, the capstone: how the whole pipeline is scored end-to-end. benchmarks/text-to-cad/specs.json holds 10 natural-language part specs with expected geometry hints, and scripts/run_benchmarks.py runs each one through cad_agent_v4 as a subprocess, derives geometry from the produced STEP, and writes timestamped pass/fail results. This is the objective measure behind the Tier 0 smoke tests promised in BUILDS.md from Step 2, closing the loop from design intent to verified output.
